newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy '98 car mkt to slump without incentives-Fiat.
newsitem.headline: Italy '98 car mkt to slump without incentives-Fiat.

text.p: The Italian car market is likely to fall to the low levels of 1996 in 1998 without the effect of a government incentive scheme for the sector, Fiat group managing director Paolo Cantarella said.
It was realistically "difficult to forecast the car market in 1998 in the absence of incentives" in Italy, Cantarella said in response to shareholders' questions at the annual general meeting here.
But he said: "It is reasonable to suppose that next year the market would not be far from levels in 1996, a year in which we had to resort to a temporary lay-off arrangement," he said.

Cantarella said that if the incentive scheme were suspended in September it would only have been in operation for nine months whereas other European countries with similar arrangements had kept them going for longer.
France adopted such a scheme for two-and-a-half years while Spain "transformed the measure from a temporary one into a structural one."
